newsitem.title: GERMANY: German drug industry faces lower sales soon.
newsitem.headline: German drug industry faces lower sales soon.

text.p: Strong sales growth in the German drug industry are likely to be capped in the next months as physicians, facing empty coffers, try to save on presciption drugs, an industry federation said on Wednesday.
"The sector is looking forward to lower sales because physicians' budgets are largely exhausted and they are being reprimanded to save," the BPI said in a statement.
During the first eight months of the 1996, the industry posted sales of 16.8 billion marks, registering a 7.4 percent increase from year-ago levels, the group said.
One reason for strong sales is that physicians tended to prefer prescribing newer and more expensive drugs and that this trend helped offset a general decline in drug prices.

But now, faced with government guidelines to adhere to preset pharmaceutical budgets which have been largely exhausted, the industry association fears that the trend of rising sales will be abruptly capped.

The industry has gone through a period of consolidation, losing some 13,000 jobs since 1993. Now the industry employs only 120,000. In June the industry workforce was 1.3 percent lower than it was a year ago.
